context: A grandpa and grandkid spend a day
purpose: Teach: 成田空港/読み手/ドラム缶/ローラ/滑る/解ける/歌え/見入っ

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、成田空港、行ったこと、ある?
lines.en: Grandpa, have you ever been to Narita Airport?
lines.style: Gentle, curious opening. Small voice. Unhurried—he's genuinely interested, not rushing for an answer. Respectful pause before the question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。物語の読み手、子供の頃から、好きだったよ。
lines.en: Yes. I've loved stories since I was your age, you know.
lines.style: Soft, distant gaze inward. A slight smile in the voice. Warm but reflective—he's traveling back in time as he speaks. Unhurried pacing.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 昔の遊び場、ドラム缶、置いてあったね、写真で。
lines.en: In that old playground photo, there were drum cans sitting around, right?
lines.style: Engaged, observant. Brighter energy—he's remembered something vivid. Not loud, but present. Small lift of discovery in his voice.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お父さんも、ローラースケート、得意だったな、若い頃。
lines.en: Your dad was good at roller skating too, back when he was young.
lines.style: Tender nostalgia. A faint smile underlying the words. Slow, measured delivery—he's holding the memory gently. Slight warmth on 「得意だったな」.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 冬の坂、滑るから、おじいちゃん、気をつけてね。
lines.en: The winter slopes are slippery, so you be careful, Grandpa.
lines.style: Small, sincere concern beneath the surface. Soft but steady. He's not lecturing—he's genuinely worried. Quiet protectiveness in the closing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。難しい問題も、ゆっくり解ける子だったよ、お父さん。
lines.en: Yes. Your dad was the kind who could solve hard problems slowly and carefully.
lines.style: Quiet pride underneath. Thoughtful, as if he's realizing something as he speaks. Slight warmth on 「難しい問題」. Slow, deliberate pacing.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、昔の歌、一緒に歌える?
lines.en: Grandpa, can we sing an old song together?
lines.style: Hopeful, bright anticipation. Small but unmistakable excitement. He's reaching out—asking something that matters. Open, inviting tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 庭の桜、毎年、見入ってしまうんだよ、私は。
lines.en: I always find myself drawn to the cherry blossoms in the garden every spring, you see.
lines.style: Warm, gentle. Slightly dreamy—not entirely present, caught in the beauty of the memory. Soft, almost conversational trailing. Voice like an old hand on a shoulder.
